title: SSC MTS and Havaldar: organise two-session practice and next-stage checks
description: Separate MTS written preparation from Havaldar physical-stage requirements, review accuracy by session and understand an additional shortlist.
intro: MTS and Havaldar share a written examination, but they do not have identical next stages. The currently covered 2025 cycle includes an additional Havaldar shortlist dated 7 October 2026. This guide helps you read that status correctly and build a useful practice routine for a future attempt.

sections.title: Label the cycle before reading a result
sections.body:
Write down examination year, post and notice date before opening a roll-number list. A notice published in October 2026 can still belong to the 2025 examination. “Additional shortlist” also does not mean every earlier outcome has been replaced.

The 7 October notice concerns additional Havaldar PET/PST processing and includes withheld and sealed-cover qualifications. Read the [published explanation](/exam-updates/ssc-mts-havaldar-2025-additional-result/) and the official write-up before deciding your status. A shortlist allows the next stated stage; it does not itself establish appointment or clear an unresolved eligibility condition.

sections.title: Keep the two sessions separate in practice
sections.body:
Read the current examination notice for the subjects, timers, minimums and marking rules of each session. Do not apply a single familiar negative-marking formula to the entire MTS paper without checking. Create separate review lines for numerical/reasoning work and for awareness/language work.

In numerical ability, practise setting up a problem before accelerating calculation. In reasoning, record the rule that justified the next term or relationship. For awareness, use closed-book recall. In language practice, explain why the rejected options fail. A balanced written score needs both understanding and reliable recall, not only many attempts.

sections.title: Use short daily sets that expose one error
sections.body:
Try one arithmetic idea, one reasoning family, one reading or grammar exercise and a small awareness recall block. If time is short, reduce the number of questions while preserving the review. Finish by retrying yesterday's mistake without the answer visible.

For example, a ratio question may fail because you used the total number as one share. Repair that with a diagram and two new examples. Continue through [ratio and proportion](/quant/ratio-proportion/) and [number series](/reasoning/series/). Keep a weekly mixed block to check whether you can recognise the method without a chapter heading.

sections.title: Prepare the correct next-stage folder
sections.body:
MTS candidates should follow the selection and document-verification instructions for their post. Havaldar candidates must additionally follow the official PET/PST notice and call letter where shortlisted. Do not assume every MTS applicant has a physical test.

Keep the application, identity details, qualification and claimed-category documents consistent. Review name or date-of-birth discrepancies early through the official process. Use the [MTS process page](/exams/ssc-mts/admit-card/) to locate the next notice. Never upload certificates or identity documents to an unofficial result-checking form.

drills.prompt: A total of 180 items is divided in the ratio 2:3. How many are in the smaller share?
drills.explanation: There are five shares. Each is 180 ÷ 5 = 36, so the smaller share is 2 × 36 = 72.

drills.prompt: An additional Havaldar PET/PST shortlist appears. Does it prove a final MTS appointment?
drills.explanation: Post, cycle, stage and conditions must all match. A next-stage shortlist is not a final appointment order.

checklist: Match the year and post in my notice.
Read any withheld or conditional-result note.
Retry one arithmetic and one reasoning error.
Prepare only the documents requested for my next stage.

sources.label: SSC official notices and candidate portal

faqs.q: Does every MTS candidate take Havaldar PET/PST?
faqs.a: No. Follow the post-specific selection stages in the current notice.

faqs.q: Should I use another SSC exam’s marking rule?
faqs.a: No. Read the MTS session and stage rules for the examination you are practising.
